newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB to issue April debentures as planned-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: NCB to issue April debentures as planned-spokesman.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd will issue its April bank debentures as planned, and will set the terms on April 9, a bank spokesman said on Wednesday.
NCB will decide the terms for its new debentures while keeping a close watch on how the market evaluates the bank's restructuring efforts, the spokesman told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The bank had no plans at present to reduce the issue of its bank debentures from the usual amount, the spokesman said.

"We are not thinking of reducing the issue amount right now. Rather, we hope the market will view our restructuring efforts positively and we hope we will be able to increase the issue amount of debentures from current levels in the future," he said.
NCB's five-year bank debentures due in June 1999 with a coupon rate of 3.5 percent were offered at 7.375 percent on Wednesday, a trader for a major brokerage house said.
The announcement of NCB's restructuring plans has not led to a significant fall in market yields of the bank's debentures so far, the trader said.
"The number of sell orders had decreased somewhat, but that's about it," the trader said.
On Tuesday, NCB's five-year debenture due in July 1999 with a coupon rate of 3.5 percent was traded at 7.0 percent.
The market is reserving judgment until it sees how the restructuring plans are put into action, he added.
NCB on Tuesday announced a major restructuring plan that will mean large loan writeoffs, the sale of prime real estate and a withdrawal from overseas markets.
The bank said it believes the scheme will help it to regain the market's trust.
